name: Cuban heel / Chelsea boots
lead: Cuban-heel Chelsea boots, often called Beatle boots, are ankle-high, close-fitting boots with elastic or zip sides, a pointed toe and a Cuban heel, a moderately raised, tapered, stacked heel.[1] In looksmaxxing and height-focused style discussion they are mentioned as footwear that adds roughly one to two inches through a built-in heel, without the visible bulk of a platform.

The Chelsea boot itself dates to the Victorian era and is credited to Joseph Sparkes Hall, shoemaker to Queen Victoria.[2] The Cuban-heeled variant became famous through The Beatles and other 1960s musicians.[1]

Published studies of how heeled boots change perceived height or attractiveness were not found for this entry. Effects described below are those reported by makers and style communities rather than tested outcomes.

paras: The classic Chelsea boot has a snug ankle, elastic side panels, a pull tab and a low heel.[2] The Beatle boot variant adds a higher Cuban heel and pointed toe, and may use zip sides instead of elastic.[1]

Vulcanised rubber made the elastic gusset possible, and the boot was fashionable by the late 1840s, remaining prominent in the West until World War I.[2] It returned in 1950s and 1960s Britain, linked to the King's Road scene and mod culture.[2]

Anello & Davide made Beatle boots in 1961 after John Lennon and Paul McCartney commissioned pairs.[2] The style was worn by Teddy Boys, beatniks and rockers, and later by punk musicians, and regained popularity in the late 2000s and early 2010s.[1]

In height-focused style advice, heeled boots are listed alongside lifts and platforms as a way to add apparent height while keeping a conventional boot silhouette. Proponents say the heel is less conspicuous than a platform sole.

timeline.event: Elastic-sided boot becomes fashionable in Britain.[2]
Anello & Davide make Beatle boots for Lennon and McCartney.[2]

card.summary: Pointed Chelsea boots with a Cuban heel, a stylish way to gain an inch or two with no study behind the claim.
card.note: Heels change gait and ankle stability; no trials on perceived-height effects.

quick.overview:
Cuban-heel Chelsea boots are close-fitting ankle boots with a modest stacked heel. They are discussed as a fashion route to a little extra height.

The style traces to the Victorian Chelsea boot and became famous via The Beatles in the 1960s.
quick.mechanism: The built-in heel raises the wearer, with makers and style communities citing about one to two inches.
quick.risks: Raised heels alter posture and ankle stability in general, and podiatrists comment on heeled footwear; no studies specific to this boot were found. The height gain lasts only while the boots are worn.
